title: Intermittent gateway latency
executive_summary:
INC-010 (SEV3, intermittent gateway latency) investigation is INCONCLUSIVE: the root cause could not be established. api-gateway p99 latency rose about 35% from a baseline of 252.9 ms to a window mean of 341.3 ms (max 557.0 ms), with onset at 19:40Z (met-api-gateway-p99_latency_ms-1930-2010). Median latency (p50 +1.2%) and request rate (-2.7%) were essentially flat, and no alarm fired. No leading hypothesis is supported. Evidence gaps are material: 24 of 41 gateway data points are missing, downstream p99 data is almost entirely absent, and deployment and config-change queries failed because the investigation tool-call budget was exhausted. Those failed queries are unverified gaps, not evidence that nothing changed.

Hypothesis status: H2 (postgres report_rollup contention) is rejected, since postgres p95, p99 and CPU were flat across the window (met-postgres-p95_latency_ms-1935-1950, met-postgres-cpu_pct-1935-1950) and the slow statement at 19:30Z precedes onset (logpat-postgres-44883ca5). H1 (slow-client uploads), H3 (upstream degradation), H4 (infrastructure event) and H5 (telemetry artifact) remain at needs_evidence with low confidence (0.0 to 0.13). The first logged slow upload (19:44Z, log-441467a5 and related) follows the 19:40Z onset, which weakens H1. H3 cannot be tested because downstream data is missing. H4 is not excluded because per-instance metrics were not pulled. H5 is plausible given the sampling gaps.

hypotheses.description: An intermittent, unobserved degradation in one of the four gateway upstreams (order, payment, auth, or user) drives the gateway tail latency. order-service is listed first only because it has the most dependency fan-out (postgres, redis, message-queue, payment, user). Mechanism: A slow subset of upstream calls holds gateway request threads longer. Because the gateway fans out to four upstreams, a single slow upstream lifts the p99 tail while p50 is unaffected.

critic_review.summary: No hypothesis is adequately supported. My attempts to pull deployments, config changes and gateway error/timeout metrics all failed with BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, so those are unverified evidence gaps, not evidence of health. What the existing evidence shows: api-gateway p99 rises about 35% from a 19:40Z onset while p50 and CPU are flat, and request rate is down 2.7%. The gateway tail is real in the metrics, but its cause is not identified. H2 is rejected: postgres p95, p99 and CPU are flat across the window and the 19:30Z statement precedes onset. H1 is weakened because the first logged slow upload is at 19:44Z, after the 19:40Z onset, and the upload WARN logs are partial and inconsistent between queries. H3 cannot be tested because downstream p99 is almost entirely missing (only the 19:30Z order-service point exists), so an upstream slowdown is neither confirmed nor excluded. H4 is weakened by flat aggregate CPU but not excluded, since per-instance data was never pulled. H5 (telemetry artifact) is plausible given 24 of 41 gateway points missing, but the 19:35 and 19:40 samples form a consistent step across retries. Further evidence requests cannot be executed in this final round with the tool budget exhausted.

assessments.reasoning: Onset at 19:40Z precedes the first logged slow upload at 19:44Z, so the logged uploads cannot explain the onset. The upload WARN logs are partial and disagree between queries. Per-route p99 or request-size data would be needed, and those queries could not be run.

Plausible tail mechanism, but no upstream p99 exists for 19:35-20:10Z beyond a single baseline-level order-service point. Neither onset nor upstream culprit can be confirmed. Upstream timing or gateway-side upstream latency would be needed.

Flat aggregate CPU argues against a broad fleet problem, but a subset-of-instances fault is not excluded. Per-instance latency and infrastructure event data were never collected, and the deployment/config check failed.

A telemetry artifact is a real possibility given heavy sparsity after 19:45Z. However, the 19:35 and 19:40 samples show a consistent step across retries, so it is not established as an artifact. Resolving the telemetry gap is needed to settle it.

postgres p95, p99 and CPU are flat across 19:35-20:10Z with no onset at 19:40Z. The only slow-statement evidence is weak, partial log data, and there is no evidence that any gateway route touches report_rollup().

conclusion: Root cause could not be conclusively established with the available evidence. INC-010 remains INCONCLUSIVE. Gateway p99 latency rose about 35% from 19:40Z while median latency and request rate were flat, and no hypothesis reached a supported status. Postgres contention has been rejected. The remaining candidates (upstream degradation, a subset-of-instance infrastructure issue, slow-client uploads, or a telemetry artifact) cannot be distinguished with current evidence, mainly because of missing downstream data and failed deployment and config queries. Priority is to close these evidence gaps (deployment/config history, per-instance metrics, and upstream latency) and to add alerting so that the next occurrence is attributable.
